notes: This touch closes out PF_STRAT.REVIEW_GATES' 'not yet audited' flag for META's 2026-07-29 print. Revenue beat (+28% YoY, $60.8B vs $60.29B consensus, ad price +12% YoY, impressions +14% YoY) but GAAP EPS missed badly ($6.18 vs $7.22, -14.4%) almost entirely on two one-time items: $2.4B legal charges + $1.18B severance (CFO said op income ex-charges was +9% YoY). The genuinely new, non-one-time part of the story: FY26 capex floor raised to $130-145B (low end raised, a locked-in commitment) while quarterly FCF collapsed to ~$0.8B. Stock fell ~9% over two sessions despite the revenue beat. Original kill-switch ('demand quality degrades into a true bear lane, OR AI monetization breaks out') did not technically fire either direction — demand held up, AI monetization stayed unquantified — but price still re-rated hard on the capex/FCF axis the original kill-switch didn't fully anticipate. Bands lowered across all three cases (multiple regime de-rated a full turn or two) but analyst 12-month price targets (avg ~$733, still Buy/Outperform-rated) cluster in the new base-to-bull range, well above the current $539 price -- the dislocation thesis persists but its cause has shifted from pure capex-fear sentiment to a partly real capex-vs-FCF tension. EU DMA: no new ruling this quarter, still an open Commission review of Meta's updated compliance model, appeal from July 2025 still pending.
